guards.guard: the roll numbers are nonetheless uncontaminated by that restart
guards.observed: MEASURED, not assumed. stats_process_local.requests held at 528 and cache_hits at 539 continuously across web's restart (samples 34->38) while builds and prepare.prepared kept climbing. A restarted process resets those counters; they did not reset. The prepare/roll machinery therefore lives on flow-worker (reached through web's proxy), which did not restart -- its apscheduler line is continuous from 12:23Z. So the roll series is a warm-process series throughout.

notes: THE HEADLINE OF THIS ITEM IS handoff_ms. Across the first ten steady rolls it read 7, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 12 ms -- max 12 ms, p50 1 ms -- and blocked_by was null on every one. Item 12 is scoped to rolls with handoff_ms > 500; at the open there were none, and nothing was ever blocked. prepare_ms: the first roll of the session cost 8242 ms, then the series settled to 434-2277 ms (p50 of the first ten ~1073 ms). The 8242 ms is the first roll after a frozen pre-open tape, i.e. the largest delta the process had to absorb, not a cold process. Three fields the run prompt asks for are NOT exposed per-roll by this endpoint -- builds, build_failures, parts_rejected_missing -- and csv_provider share is not exposed at all; the cumulative counters are given instead and the gap is named rather than filled.
